item.title: Invariant von Neumann subalgebras of crossed products and tensor products
item.description: arXiv:2610.19023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a countable discrete group acting on a tracial von Neumann algebra $(Q,\tau_Q)$ in a trace-preserving way. We study invariant von Neumann subalgebras of $Q\rtimes\Gamma$ and of $L(\Gamma)\bar\otimes Q$, where the latter is equipped with the diagonal action. We show that, under the pointwise weak mixing assumption, an invariant subalgebra whose image under the canonical conditional expectation onto $Q$ is scalar is necessarily contained in $L(\Gamma)$. Further, under relative weak mixing and central freeness assumptions, we determine the structure of invariant subalgebras of the crossed product with non-trivial intersection with $Q$. For p.m.p. actions of groups with trivial amenable radical and the invariant subalgebras rigidity property, pointwise relative weak mixing gives a complete classification of invariant subalgebras in the tensor product case. We construct essentially free, prime, pointwise weakly mixing p.m.p. actions of $\mathbb{F}_n$ for every $2\leq n\leq\infty$, as well as non-prime examples with explicitly described factors.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Artem Dudko, Yongle Jiang, Adam Skalski

item.title: On the Isomorphism of Semicircular Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.19590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on OpenAI's proof of isomorphism of free group factors, we give a self-contained proof of a corresponding result for $C^{*}$-algebras generated by free semicircular systems: the isomorphism class of a $C^{*}$-algebra generated by a semicircular $n$-tuple does not depend on $n\in\{2,3,\dots,+\infty\}$. Similarly, reduced free products of $n$ copies of the Jiang--Su algebra are isomorphic for different $n$ in this range. While reduced free group $C^{*}$-algebras of different ranks are not isomorphic (by a result of Pimsner--Voiculescu), we show that they have strong free absorption properties. At the heart of the proof is an automorphism approximation property for inclusions of $C^{*}$- and $W^{*}$-algebras; a relative version of that property was previously used to derive free complementation results.
item.dc:creator: D. Shlyakhtenko

item.title: Spectral truncations of SU(2) and the spectral localizer
item.description: arXiv:2610.19791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study operator systems arising from Peter-Weyl and Dirac spectral truncations of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ in the sense of Connes-Van Suijlekom. We determine operator system invariants for these systems, including the $C^*$-envelope and uniform bounds on the propagation number. For Peter-Weyl truncations, we find $\mathrm{prop} \leq 2$ for all connected compact Lie groups, generalizing known results for the torus. We also carry out an analysis of the spectral localizer by Loring and Schulz-Baldes on $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. In this analysis, we find numerical evidence that an index map for operator systems previously proposed by Van Suijlekom only captures the right information in a suitable interval of the parameter $\kappa$, instead of the limit $\kappa \downarrow 0$.
item.dc:creator: Matt Verhoeven

item.title: Cwikel estimates and Weyl's laws for $L\log L$ potentials on quantum tori
item.description: arXiv:2610.20373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an \(L\log L\)-endpoint Cwikel estimate on quantum tori $\mathbb T_\theta^d$, i.e., for every \(d\geq 1\) and \(x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)\), \begin{equation*} (1-\Delta)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\lambda(x)(1-\Delta)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\in\mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} \end{equation*} with a bound depending only on the dimension, where $\lambda(x)$ is the left multiplication by $x$. The main ingredient is an abstract weak Hilbert--Schmidt estimate for multiplication operators in finite von Neumann algebras whose \(L_2\)-spaces admit orthonormal bases of unitaries. When $\theta=0$, our argument also gives a simpler proof of the $L\log L$ Cwikel estimate on classical tori. For $d\geq2$, we use the $C^*$-algebraic principal symbol map to prove Weyl's laws for finite sums \[ \sum_{\ell=1}^N S_\ell(1-\Delta)^{-d/4}\lambda(x_\ell) (1-\Delta)^{-d/4}T_\ell, \] where $x_\ell\in L\log L(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$ and $S_\ell,T_\ell\in\Pi$, the $C^*$-algebra generated by $\lambda(C(\mathbb T_\theta^d))$ and Fourier multipliers with continuous symbols homogeneous of degree zero. We also prove a semiclassical Weyl's law for critical Schr\"odinger operators with $L\log L$ potentials.
item.dc:creator: Siyu Liu, Xinyu Zhang

item.title: Maximal subgroups of topological full groups of shifts of finite type
item.description: arXiv:2610.20024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study maximal subgroups of topological full groups of irreducible one-sided shifts of finite type whose associated groupoids have Cantor unit space. For each wide open subgroupoid of such a groupoid, we construct a subgroupoid graph and identify the subgroupoid with a full compact open reduction of the corresponding countable graph groupoid. Every minimal wide open subgroupoid is either AF or purely infinite. A proper wide open subgroupoid is prime if it admits no proper intermediate wide open subgroupoid. We prove a trichotomy for prime subgroupoids: they are minimal, arise from a clopen bipartition, or have a unique nonempty proper closed invariant set, which is nowhere dense. For a prime subgroupoid, the normalizer of its topological full group is maximal in the ambient topological full group precisely when it maps onto the ambient abelianization. An analogous criterion holds in every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup. For a minimal prime subgroupoid, its topological full group is maximal precisely when it equals its normalizer and the inclusion induces a surjection on first groupoid homology. We also describe all fully amplified maximal subgroups, namely those closed under local agreement. For Thompson's group $V$, the stabilizer of every simple type system is maximal, extending results of Belk, Bleak, Quick and Skipper for finite type systems and certain classes of infinite ones. Finally, every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup has continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic maximal subgroups acting minimally on the unit space.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matui

item.title: Von Neumann Type Inequalities for NC Operator Balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.20355v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish finite-dimensional von Neumann type inequalities for commuting matrix tuples in noncommutative operator balls. Let $\Omega=\mathbb{D}_Q$ be the NC operator ball of a linear pencil $Q$ with linearly independent coefficients. If $\Omega(1)$ admits a transitive subgroup of automorphisms with NC lifts and $\Omega(1)$ has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, then $\|f(T)\|\leq C_{\Omega,n}\|f\|_{H^\infty(\Omega(1))}$ for every commuting tuple $T\in\Omega(n)$, with $C_{\Omega,n}=(2\rho_{\Omega}K_{\Omega})^{n-1}$; here $K_{\Omega}$ is the Gleason constant and $\rho_{\Omega}$ is the sum of the suprema of the coordinate functions on $\Omega(1)$. The scalar coordinate bounds persist at every matrix level. The hypotheses hold for products of row and column balls, where $\rho_{\Omega}=d$, yielding an unconditional estimate $(2dK_{\Omega})^{n-1}$. For a general type I Cartan domain $R_{p,q}$, we obtain only a conditional result: the same bound holds provided the scalar domain has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, which we do not establish when $\min(p,q)\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Ran Kiri

item.title: Solution to Dixmier's Problem about spectra of C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.26319v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dixmier asked in 1967 whether the spectra of simple separable non-type-I $C^*$-algebras all have the same Borel structure. We solve the formulation using ordinary isomorphisms of quotient Borel $\sigma$-algebras by proving that its universal assertion is independent of ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC. Under the continuum hypothesis, all separable non-type-I spectra are measurably isomorphic, without simplicity or unitality assumptions. In the model obtained by iterating Sacks forcing for $\omega_2$ stages with countable supports over a GCH ground model, a fixed simple unital universal spectrum is not measurably isomorphic to the CAR spectrum. Neither consistency direction requires a large cardinal. The Borel-definable formulation, which requires isomorphisms to admit Borel lifts between irreducible representations, has a negative answer in ZFC. For the CAR algebra $A$ and a simple separable exact crossed product $B$ associated to $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$, there is no Borel-definable injection $\widehat B\to\widehat A$. Nevertheless, all separable nuclear non-type-I spectra are Borel-definably isomorphic. We also determine the answer under several choiceless hypotheses. The axiom of determinacy together with dependent choice gives a stronger negative conclusion: the spectrum of $B$ does not even inject as a set into the spectrum of $A$. The symmetric Solovay model gives the same conclusion. Over ZF, a wellordering of the reals of order type $\omega_1$ suffices for a positive answer. The finite-permutation Feferman--Levy model gives another positive answer for the full sigma-generated Borel structures. These comparisons concern the quotient structures themselves, without measure completion.
item.dc:creator: Martino Lupini

item.title: Aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.17543v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We completely classify aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra $\mathcal{W}$ up to outer conjugacy. As a technical ingredient, based on the works of Connes, Herman--Ocneanu, Kishimoto, and Sato, we introduce a notion of weak stability for automorphisms of simple separable monotracial C$^*$-algebras. We also consider automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type and the Jiang--Su algebra. In particular, we classify aperiodic ``UHF-absorbing'' automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type up to outer conjugacy.
item.dc:creator: Norio Nawata

item.title: Non-Archimedean Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrodinger and Non-Archimedean Maccone-Pati Uncertainty Principles
item.description: arXiv:2505.02838v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a non-Archimedean Hilbert space over a conjugated non-Archimedean valued field $\mathbb{K}$ with $\operatorname{Char}(\mathbb{K})\neq 2$. Let $A: \mathcal{D}(A)\subseteq \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{X}$ and $B: \mathcal{D}(B)\subseteq \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{X}$ be possibly unbounded self-adjoint linear operators. For $x \in \mathcal{D}(A)$ with $\langle x, x \rangle =1$, define $ \Delta _x(A):= \|Ax- \langle Ax, x \rangle x \|.$ Then for all $x \in \mathcal{D}(AB)\cap \mathcal{D}(BA)$ with $\langle x, x \rangle =1$, we show that \begin{align*} (1) \quad \Delta_x(A)+\Delta_x(B)\geq \max\{\Delta_x(A), \Delta_x(B)\}\geq \frac{\sqrt{\bigg|\big\langle [A,B]x, x \big\rangle ^2+\big(\langle \{A,B\}x, x \rangle -2\langle Ax, x \rangle\langle Bx, x \rangle\big)^2\bigg|}}{\sqrt{|2|}} \end{align*} and \begin{align*} (2) \quad \Delta_x(A)+\Delta_x(B)\geq \max\{\Delta_x(A), \Delta_x(B)\} \geq |\langle (A+B)x, y \rangle |, \quad \forall y \in \mathcal{X} \text{ satisfying } \|y\|\leq 1, \langle x, y \rangle =0. \end{align*} Inequality (1) may be regarded as a non-Archimedean analogue of the Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrodinger uncertainty principle, while Inequality (2) serves as a non-Archimedean analogue of the Maccone-Pati uncertainty principle.
item.dc:creator: K. Mahesh Krishna
